UI_QuickRestart_Memory_Info:
There is currently a bug in Project Zomboid: it cannot release all of the memory it uses between games. After a given number of restarts, it adds up and can cause in-game errors or even hard crashes. The number of zombies is the main factor but not the only one: the higher it is, the quicker the memory fills up. This happens with or without Quick Restart.

The number of restarts left is measured from how fast the memory fills up on your machine, with your mods and your settings. It is approximate, and it gets more accurate the longer you play. With the sandbox or zombie randomizer enabled, it is far less reliable, since each world can consume a very different amount of memory.

Every time a new world starts loading, Quick Restart checks how much memory the game is still using. The gap between two worlds is what one restart costs you. It also keeps a bit of spare room, because the game usually crashes before the memory is really full. How much room it keeps depends on your mods and your randomizer choices, and each combination gets its own number. If a crash happens without enough warning, it keeps more room next time. If it warns you way too early, it keeps less. If you change how much memory the game is allowed to use, Quick Restart notices and adapts after a couple of restarts.

Quick Restart will not be able to catch every crash, but it will tell you as early as it can, every time it sees the memory leak acting up. The issue has already been reported on the Project Zomboid forum, hopefully the developers will fix it as soon as possible.

Please feel free to provide any feedback on this feature.

Thank you for enjoying Quick Restart.

OhHoop
Mod creator
